fields.source: OpenBSD pledge(2) design grammar extended to MASTER
fields.ask: Can a capability context regain authority after it has been dropped or locked? Reduced contexts must remain reduced; new authority requires a new trusted context.
fields.fix: Do not reacquire capabilities. Create a new trusted context when a genuinely different authority set is required.

fields.source: pub4 commerce boundary — BRGEN owns listings/orders; Amber owns wardrobe intelligence
fields.fix: Consume the public Shared::Commerce/BRGEN catalog contract through BrgenCommerce; do not load BRGEN models.

fields.source: pub4 commerce boundary — Amber owns wardrobe intelligence; BRGEN owns transactions
fields.fix: Keep wardrobe ranking and wardrobe records in Amber; expose only commerce references and catalog facts across the boundary.

fields.source: pub4 commerce protocol — external inventory must carry source and provenance
fields.fix: Use ShopTheLook::Suggestion with source, reasons, and commerce_key so a commercial recommendation is attributable and explainable.
fields.good: Suggestion.new(title, merchant, url, "brgen", score, reasons, commerce_key)

fields.source: CSS fluid typography — clamp() (web.dev)
fields.fix: Use font-size: clamp(1rem, 2.5vw, 1.5rem).

fields.source: CSS Logical Properties and Values (W3C)
fields.fix: Use margin-inline-start/end, padding-inline-start/end.

fields.source: Bringhurst, Elements of Typographic Style — the measure (45–75 chars)
fields.fix: Bound running-text columns to ~66ch (≈ 33rem), not wide px values.

fields.source: Mobile First (Luke Wroblewski, 2011)
fields.fix: Use min-width (mobile-first, progressive enhancement).

fields.source: Sass best practice — @use over @import (Sass team)
fields.fix: @import is deprecated. Use @use/@forward.

fields.source: style.yml motion budget / FrontendLawSet MOTION
fields.fix: Keep transitions ≤300ms.

fields.source: MASTER-native (one language per file)
fields.ask: Does this file embed multiple languages or notations, or does the artifact mix incompatible frameworks or media layers?
fields.fix: One language per layer. Separate into distinct files or clearly demarcated sections.
fields.bad:
good "rows = connection.exec(query)" end # Every Layout (Bell & Pickering): let the content size the box. A fixed pixel # height on a container is a promise about content the container cannot keep — # text wraps, translations run long (Norwegian does), and the box clips or # spills. min-height states the same floor without the ceiling. Below 100px # the element is a control or a media frame sizing itself, not a text # container, so the law starts where flowing content starts. # # The book's other axiom — space between siblings belongs to the parent (gap), # not the children (margin-bottom chains) — is not per-line decidable: whether # a margin is a chain depends on the siblings, which only the rendered tree # knows. It stays a review judgment, not a detector. Law.define(:FIXED_HEIGHT) do source "Every Layout (Bell & Pickering) — the content sizes the box" severity :info languages %i[css scss] # A drawn stage — an art frame, a product-photo crop window — sizes itself # by contract, not by its content. Those lines carry scan: intentional with # the reason; the marker keeps the law on flowing-content boxes. detect { |line| line.match?(/(?|>>|>>|▸|▸|▸)" unless const_defined?(:ARROW_GLYPH) DOT_GLYPH = "(?:·|·|·|·)" unless const_defined?(:DOT_GLYPH) # The innermost { … } blocks of a stylesheet, with their selector. def blocks(text) text.scan(/([^{};]*)\{([^{}]*)\}/m).map { |selector, body| [selector.strip, body] } end # px / rem / em value under the body size, or a named small step. def small_size?(body) value = body[/font-size\s*:\s*([^;}\n]+)/i, 1].to_s.strip return false if value.empty? return true if value.match?(/(?:--|\$)(?:font-?(?:size-?)?)?(?:2?xs|sm|small|caption|label|micro|tiny)\b/i) number = value[/\A([\d.]+)(rem|em|px)\b/i, 1] return false unless number value.match?(/px\b/i) ? number.to_f < 16 : number.to_f < 1 end # Tracked all-caps eyebrows: uppercase and non-zero tracking together, on text # that is small or that the author named an eyebrow, kicker or overline. def eyebrow_blocks(text) blocks(text).select do |selector, body| next false unless body.match?(/text-transform\s*:\s*uppercase/i) # Heading case is structural, not a decorative label treatment. A heading # remains a finding even when it is large or has no tracking; proper case # is consistent across the levels and the page H1 carries the hierarchy. heading = selector.match?(/(?:\A|[\s,>])h[1-6](?=$|[\s,.:#\[])/i) || selector.match?(/\.(?:page-title|section-title|empty-state-title|luxury-title|amber-look-title|store-heading)\b/i) next true if heading next false unless body.match?(/letter-spacing\s*:\s*+(?!0(?:\.0+)?(?:px|r?em)?\s*[;}\n]|normal|inherit|initial|unset)[^;}\n]+/i) selector.match?(/eyebrow|kicker|overline/i) || small_size?(body) end end def eyebrow_class?(line) = line.match?(/class\s*[:=]\s*["'][^"']*\b(?:eyebrow|kicker|overline)\b/i) # A glyph that points at the next step, appended to the label of a link or button. def arrow_label?(line) return true if line.match?(%r{<(?:a|button)\b[^>]*>[^<]*?\s#{ARROW_GLYPH}\s*}i) return true if line.match?(%r{]*>\s*#{ARROW_GLYPH}\s*}i) line.match?(/\b(?:link_to|button_to|submit|link_to_if)\b\s*\(?\s*(["'])[^"']*?\S\s*#{ARROW_GLYPH}\s*\1/) end # `A · B · C`: two or more dot separators between words, or a join(" · "). def dotted_meta?(line) return false if line.match?(/= 2 end # A gradient painted as a surface. A fade to transparent is a functional edge # (a scroll hint, a scrim under text), so it is spared, as is a mask, a solid # fill and a hard-stop data bar. def gradient_wash?(line) return false unless line.match?(/(?:background(?:-image)?|--[\w-]+)\s*:[^;]*(?:linear|radial|conic)-gradient\(/i) return false if line.match?(/transparent|\bmask/i) # A colour used twice is a hard stop or a solid fill: a hairline or a data bar. !line.scan(/var\(--[\w-]+\)|#\h{3,8}\b/).tally.value?(2) end # Leading-zero counters and literal 0N labels: ornament on items that need no order. def ordinal_ornament?(line) return true if line.match?(/counter\([^)]*decimal-leading-zero/i) return true if line.match?(/content\s*:\s*["']0\d\b/) return true if line.match?(/>\s*0[1-9]\s*[\/.]?\s*Les mer →' good 'Les saken' end Law.define(:NO_DOT_SEPARATED_META) do source "LINEARITY — structure belongs to the element tree; glyphs between words make a flat string the reader must parse" severity :info languages %i[html] detect { |line| DesignMarks.dotted_meta?(line) } fix "Put each fact in its own element (a list item or a span) and let spacing or a border separate them." bad "

Bergen · 3 timer siden · 12 svar

" good "
  • Bergen

  • 12 svar
" end Law.define(:NO_DECORATIVE_GRADIENT) do source "RENDERED_VALUES and flat design — a gradient wash is a colour the operator did not choose; surfaces are flat tokens" severity :info languages %i[css scss] detect { |line| DesignMarks.gradient_wash?(line) } fix "Paint the surface with its token colour. A fade to transparent over an edge or a scrim under text is allowed." bad ".hero { background: linear-gradient(135deg, var(--a), var(--b)); }" good ".hero { background: var(--surface); }" end Law.define(:NO_ORDINAL_ORNAMENT) do source "LINEARITY — a 01, 02, 03 marker promises a sequence; on items with no order it is decoration" severity :info languages %i[css scss html] detect { |line| DesignMarks.ordinal_ornament?(line) } fix "Drop the number, or make the items an ordered list when the order is real." bad ".card::before { content: counter(card, decimal-leading-zero); }" good "ol.steps li::marker { content: counter(list-item) \". \"; }" end Law.define(:SIGNAL_COLOR_IS_SEMANTIC) do source "pub4 visual identity contract — signal colour is a semantic marker, never a general surface or body-text colour" severity :warn languages %i[css scss] scope :file detect do |text| unsafe_signal_background = text.scan(/([^{}]+)\{([^{}]*)\}/m).any? do |selector, declarations| next false unless declarations.match?(/(?:\A|;)\s*background(?:-color)?\s*:\s*var\(\s*--pub4-signal\s*\)/i) !selector.strip.match?(/\A#cmd-palette-list\s+li\[data-active\s*=\s*["']?1["']?\]\z/i) end direct_signal_text = text.scan(/([^{}]+)\{([^{}]*)\}/m).any? do |_selector, declarations| declarations.match?(/(?:\A|;)\s*color\s*:\s*var\(\s*--pub4-signal\s*\)\s*(?:!important\s*)?;/i) end unsafe_signal_background || direct_signal_text end fix "Use the signal only as a selected-state marker with explicit signal ink; use the local product accent for ordinary buttons, page surfaces and text." bad <<~CSS .hero { background: var(--pub4-signal); color: var(--pub4-signal); } CSS good <<~CSS #cmd-palette-list li[data-active="1"] { background: var(--pub4-signal); color: var(--pub4-signal-ink); } .home-feed-view.is-active { border-block-end-color: var(--pub4-signal); } .page { background: var(--surface); color: var(--text); } CSS end

fields.source: Every Layout (Bell & Pickering) — the content sizes the box
fields.fix: Use min-height for a floor, or let the content size the box.

fields.source: Modern CSS intrinsic layout — web.dev Learn CSS
fields.ask: Does the layout solve content and component sizing with fixed dimensions or breakpoint patches where intrinsic sizing could express the relationship?
fields.fix: Prefer min/max-content, fit-content, auto, flex/grid, clamp(), and content-sized controls before adding fixed dimensions or breakpoint overrides.

fields.source: CSS Container Queries — web.dev Learn CSS
fields.ask: Does a reusable component respond to the viewport even though its actual constraint is the size of its containing component?
fields.fix: Use a named or nearest container query when the component's behavior depends on container size.

fields.source: CSS field-sizing — Baseline 2026
fields.ask: Does a form control use brittle fixed sizing where its content, label, validation state, or user input should determine its size?
fields.fix: Prefer intrinsic form sizing and field-sizing when it improves the control without harming predictability.

fields.source: Popover and dialog — web.dev Learn CSS
fields.ask: Does the interface recreate a disclosure, popover, or dialog primitive with unnecessary custom state and positioning?
fields.fix: Prefer semantic dialog, popover, details, and native open-state behavior when their contracts match the interaction.

fields.source: CSS Anchor Positioning — web.dev Learn CSS
fields.ask: Is a floating element positioned relative to another element through brittle coordinates or JavaScript when their spatial relationship is stable?
fields.fix: Prefer declarative anchor positioning where browser support and the interaction contract permit it.

fields.source: CSS @scope — Baseline 2026
fields.ask: Can a component's styles leak across unrelated DOM regions because its selectors are broader than its ownership boundary?
fields.fix: Prefer component-local selectors or @scope where it removes selector leakage without adding unnecessary abstraction.

fields.source: Modern viewport units — web platform
fields.ask: Does a mobile layout assume a stable viewport height when browser chrome, safe areas, or the virtual keyboard can change the available space?
fields.fix: Use svh, dvh, lvh, env(safe-area-inset-*), and intrinsic layout according to the actual interaction requirement.

fields.source: CSS overflow and modern scroll containers — web.dev Learn CSS
fields.ask: Does the layout create accidental page overflow, nested scroll traps, or a scroll container that breaks sticky or touch interaction?
fields.fix: Give each scroll container one intentional axis and verify the rendered scroll and sticky behavior at mobile widths.

fields.source: Web accessibility and reduced motion — web.dev
fields.ask: Does motion ignore the user's reduced-motion preference or animate a state whose continuity can be communicated without motion?
fields.fix: Respect prefers-reduced-motion and keep transitions short, purposeful, and nonessential.

fields.source: View Transitions and Navigation API — Baseline 2026
fields.ask: Does a same-origin navigation or state transition unnecessarily destroy context when continuity would make the relationship between states clearer?
fields.fix: Preserve scroll, focus, state, and visual continuity first; use View Transitions or the Navigation API only when they simplify a real transition.

fields.source: Web rendering performance — compositor-safe interaction motion
fields.ask: Does frequent interaction motion stay on transform and opacity where possible, avoid layout properties such as top/width/height, and avoid permanent will-change or expensive visual effects?
fields.fix: Animate transform and opacity for interaction feedback; let layout properties remain stable, and add will-change only around a measured animation boundary when it removes a real hitch.
fields.good: .card { transition: transform var(--duration-m3-short) var(--ease-m3-spring), opacity var(--transition-fast) var(--ease-out); }

fields.source: Interaction feedback — loading, success and failure are observable states
fields.ask: Does an action expose a coherent state sequence such as idle → working → success/failure, with the final state remaining understandable after motion stops? Do not rely on color, motion, or a short-lived flash as the only evidence.
fields.fix: Give each important action an explicit state, choreograph its transition with the shared motion tokens, and keep a static success or failure representation for reduced motion.
fields.bad: Tap Pay; briefly spin; disappear with no persistent result.
fields.good: Tap Pay → working state → self-drawing success mark or persistent failure state; all meanings remain available without motion.

fields.source: Pointer Events and touch-action — gesture ownership
fields.ask: Does a drag or swipe surface explicitly declare which pan remains with the browser and which axis belongs to the interaction? A direct-manipulation gesture must not compete silently with page scrolling, navigation gestures, or pull-to-refresh.
fields.fix: Declare touch-action on the gesture surface: use pan-y for horizontal swipes in a vertical page, pan-x for vertical rails, or none when the interaction deliberately owns both axes. Keep an equivalent keyboard/control path.

fields.source: DENSITY — a small tracked all-caps line above a heading restates the heading's role; Strunk, omit needless words
fields.fix: Drop the eyebrow; let the heading and the page structure say where the reader is. A label that names a field stays.

fields.source: DENSITY — a link already says it can be followed; an arrow glyph in its text adds no information
fields.fix: Write the verb and the object ("Les saken"); the link styling carries the affordance.

fields.source: LINEARITY — structure belongs to the element tree; glyphs between words make a flat string the reader must parse
fields.fix: Put each fact in its own element (a list item or a span) and let spacing or a border separate them.

fields.source: RENDERED_VALUES and flat design — a gradient wash is a colour the operator did not choose; surfaces are flat tokens
fields.fix: Paint the surface with its token colour. A fade to transparent over an edge or a scrim under text is allowed.

fields.source: LINEARITY — a 01, 02, 03 marker promises a sequence; on items with no order it is decoration
fields.fix: Drop the number, or make the items an ordered list when the order is real.

fields.source: pub4 visual identity contract — signal colour is a semantic marker, never a general surface or body-text colour
fields.fix: Use the signal only as a selected-state marker with explicit signal ink; use the local product accent for ordinary buttons, page surfaces and text.

fields.source: MASTER post-incident /fix hardening — finite convergence ranks
fields.fix: Use a finite sentinel or score_value before integer coercion; never call to_i/to_int on a non-finite float.

fields.source: MASTER post-incident /fix hardening — extract-then-match regex integrity
fields.fix: Match the extracted regex body with regex syntax appropriate to the body; do not add source-level escaping twice.

fields.source: WAI-ARIA (W3C) — roles for interactive elements
fields.fix: Add role= and tabindex= for accessibility.

fields.source: HTML5 semantics / WCAG 1.3.1 — an element with no meaning carries none
fields.fix: Name the group with a semantic element, or drop the wrapper and select its children by structure.

fields.source: style.yml bare_tag_targeting — no BEM in ERB
fields.fix: Target bare tags in SCSS; remove __block__element classes from ERB.

fields.source: Strunk & White I.1 — vigorous writing is concise, and so is its spacing
fields.fix: Collapse consecutive blank lines to one.

fields.source: WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices — button vs link (W3C)
fields.fix: Use <button>. Accessible by default.

fields.source: style.yml bare_tag_targeting — the tag is already the name
fields.fix: Drop the filler class and select the bare tag; a prefix that names which of several coexisting elements this is may stay.

fields.source: Rails i18n best practice (no hardcoded strings)
fields.fix: Replace literal with t('.key').

fields.source: HTML Living Standard — meta charset utf-8 (WHATWG)
fields.fix: Add a UTF-8 charset declaration as the first element in head.

fields.source: CSP script-src / separation of concerns — assets are files
fields.fix: Move it to an asset file and reference it with javascript_include_tag or stylesheet_link_tag.

fields.source: CSP / separation of concerns — no inline styles
fields.fix: Extract to CSS class; pass dynamic values as custom properties.

fields.source: RAILS/__shared frontend convention
fields.fix: Replace the selector call with a Stimulus target or querySelector.

fields.source: CSS naming — classes name meaning, not appearance
fields.fix: Name the role, not the rendering — or use the element that already means it (small, strong, em, time).

fields.source: HTML5 semantics / WCAG 1.3.1 (W3C)
fields.fix: Use <header>, <footer>, <nav>, <main>, <aside>, <article>, <section>.

fields.source: WCAG 2.4.1 Bypass Blocks / style.yml accessibility
fields.fix: Add a skip link to #main-content in the layout.

fields.source: style.yml html.forbidden.framework_class_explosion
fields.fix: Move layout to SCSS with bare tag targeting.

fields.source: MASTER/data/inter_model.yml — machine-validated peer-model exchanges
fields.ask:
Do every MASTER-to-model council turn use InterModelContract to construct a structured request envelope,
attach a SHA-256 artifact reference, validate the returned JSON finding schema, and record a bounded metric
without persisting raw model text? Invalid output must receive one structured rejection and one retry only.
fields.practice: Treat other models as protocol peers: explicit authority, evidence, bounded artifacts, structured disagreement, and no reciprocal persona.
fields.fix: Wrap every council model request with InterModelContract and validate its returned structured findings before aggregation.
